⏺ The Sea Keeps Its Own Counsel

  Before the first town learned to count its days,
  the sea was already counting, slow and wide,
  sorting the moon's pale coins along the shore
  and handing them back, one wave at a time.

  It does not hurry. It has no need to.
  Mountains rise and fold themselves to dust,
  but the water keeps its patient rhythm,
  pulling and releasing, pulling and releasing.

  Children run to it with buckets and bold hands
  and learn, in one bright afternoon, what it takes.
  A sandcastle is a promise the tide will break.
  The sea does not apologize. It simply arrives.

  Sailors have bargained with it for ten thousand years,
  offering timber, oil, and prayers in tarred bottles,
  and it has
